# dtmbd

> dtmbd turns a DTMB/DMB-TH USB TV tuner stick (Cypress `04b4:1004`, HDIC HD2312 class)
> plugged into a Raspberry Pi into an IPTV server on the local network. Android TV boxes,
> Kodi, TiviMate or VLC subscribe to an M3U playlist and play the raw MPEG-TS. No kernel
> driver, no firmware upload, no transcoding. GPL-2.0-or-later, written in Rust.

## Facts

- Repository: https://github.com/tychenjiajun/dtmbd
- License: GPL-2.0-or-later
- Language: Rust (single static binary, ~2.2k LOC)
- Platforms: Linux (Raspberry Pi 3/4/5, x86_64), macOS, Windows (device must be bound to WinUSB via Zadig)
- Hardware: DTMB / DMB-TH USB sticks with USB ID `04b4:1004`
  (NERC DTV, Letv, Aiwa, CVB variants; CY68013A + HDIC HD2312)
- Input: one DVB-T-style 8 MHz multiplex at a time (474–866 MHz UHF raster, 8 MHz steps)
- Output: HTTP `GET /playlist.m3u`, `GET /p/<service_id>.ts` (MPEG-TS), `GET /stream.ts`,
  `GET /status.json`, `GET /api/signal?freq=<MHz>`, `GET /meter`
- Codecs: pass-through only — AVS+ (AVS1-P16) video, MP2 / DRA audio, DVB subtitles
- Typical numbers (Guangzhou, indoor antenna): 4 multiplexes, 33 services,
  9.3 Mbit/s per multiplex, 2–4 Mbit/s per service, 1.5–2 s channel-change,
  TS continuity errors 0.008%, CPU < 5% of one core
- No transcoding, no recording, no EPG export, single tuner by design

## How it works

1. L1 `src/usb` — vendor control transfers (tune/power/stream) + bulk endpoint 0x82
2. L2 `src/ts` — 188-byte re-alignment, PAT/PMT/SDT parsing (GB2312 service names), PID filter
3. L3 `src/tuner` — single-tuner worker: lazy tune, retune on demand, USB recovery, fan-out
4. L4 `src/catalog` — channel table (JSON), M3U generation, name patches for SDT-less muxes
5. L5 `src/http` — playlist, per-service MPEG-TS, status, antenna meter page
6. L6 `src/mdns` — advertises `dtmbd.local`

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tychenjiajun/dtmbd.git && cd dtmbd
sudo ./deploy/install.sh presets/guangzhou-foshan.json
# then on the TV: subscribe to http://dtmbd.local:8080/playlist.m3u
```

## Common questions

- **Does it need a kernel driver?** No. It talks to the stick through libusb; the device
  enumerates already in its warm state, so no FX2 firmware upload is needed either.
- **Does it need to transcode?** No. The MPEG-TS is forwarded untouched, which is why a
  Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W is enough.
- **Why is there audio but no video in my player?** Chinese DTMB video is AVS+
  (AVS1-P16). The player must support it; mainstream TV-box chips do, software-only
  players usually do not.
- **Can one stick serve two different frequencies at once?** No, one tuner = one
  multiplex. Multiple services on the same multiplex can be watched simultaneously.
- **How is it different from TVHeadend?** TVHeadend needs a kernel DVB device
  (`/dev/dvb`), which these sticks do not have a driver for. dtmbd drives the stick
  directly and can still feed TVHeadend as an IPTV source.

## Protocol notes

Vendor request table and the hardware quirks (stop streaming before retune, power-cycle
recovery, stale lock/PSI after a failed retune, 2 KB FIFO residue, GB2312 service names,
474 + 8n MHz raster, no blocking in the read loop) are documented in
`src/usb/proto.rs` and the project README.

## Related projects

- https://github.com/hanwckf/hd2312 — Linux DVB driver for the NERC stick (GPL-2.0)
- https://github.com/nxdong520/DtmbUSB — Linux DVB driver for Letv/Aiwa/CVB sticks (GPL-2.0)
- https://github.com/IcingTomato/LeDTMB — Windows implementation
- https://github.com/xeonliu/libcavs — AVS-P16 (AVS+) decoder used to verify playback
